newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends down on selling, weak Japan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends down on selling, weak Japan.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Wednesday on the back of selling in the local exchange and the weak finish of Japanese prices, dealers said.
"The market was slightly easier when prices in Japan went down. Some people were also closing their positions and engaged in a bit of selling," a local rubber trader said.
Tokyo's benchmark May contract shed 1.4 yen to settle at 143.5 while Kobe's May contract finished at 144.0 yen, down 1.4 yen from the previous day's settlement of 145.4.
Volumes were thin. The most actively traded month was the nearby January RSS3 contract with about 765 tonnes sold.
In comparison, more than 1,900 tonnes of the December and January RSS3 rubber contract in the local exchange was sold yesterday in the market.
"Trading was really thin all around," one trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 125.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.25 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 180.00-182.00 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.30) a kg from the previous 182.00 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 175.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25) a kg from 175.75 cents.
